# Logflare (`logflare-logflare`)

Streamline your log management with Logflare! Integrate effortlessly, visualize in your browser, and leverage your existing BigQuery setup for seamless data insights. Elevate logging today!

[Service documentation](https://docs.osaas.io/osaas.wiki/Service%3A-Logflare.html) · [Source](https://github.com/Logflare/logflare)

## Example

```terraform
resource "osc_instance" "example" {
  service_id = "logflare-logflare"
  name       = "mylogflare"

  parameters = {
    PostgresBackendUrl = "..."
    SecretKeyBase      = "..."
    # DbSchema           = "..."
    # DbEncryptionKey    = "..."
    # ApiKey             = "..."
    # PublicAccessToken  = "..."
    # PrivateAccessToken = "..."
  }
}
```

Commented lines are optional parameters. Values marked `"..."` need a real value. Outputs are `url`, `external_ip`, `external_port` and the raw `instance` document, see the `osc_instance` resource.

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `PostgresBackendUrl` | string | yes | URL endpoint for external service |
| `SecretKeyBase` | string | yes |  |
| `DbSchema` | string | no | Database connection configuration |
| `DbEncryptionKey` | string | no | Database connection configuration |
| `ApiKey` | string | no | API key for authentication |
| `PublicAccessToken` | string | no | Logging or debugging configuration |
| `PrivateAccessToken` | string | no | Logging or debugging configuration |

The instance `name` must match `^\w+$` and be unique per service within the workspace. OSC lowercases it and allows at most 20 characters.

Parameter values are strings; booleans take `"true"` or `"false"`. Reference an `osc_secret` as `osc_secret.<name>.ref` to keep a value out of the instance configuration. This page is generated from the OSC catalog; the provider validates against the live catalog when planning.
